findings.title: Sensor-gap advisor reads unpublished power series; house-power gap is always 0.00 SEK/month
findings.claim: SensorGapAdvisorSensor reads coordinator.data['house_power_series'] and ['heat_pump_power_series'], but _build_data_dict never writes either key, so on a real install the missing house-power meter always ranks 0.00 SEK/month instead of the ~30.00 the series would price.
findings.mechanism: sensor.py:2825-2826 reads house_power_series/heat_pump_power_series from coordinator.data; topology.rank_sensor_gaps -> peak_miss_sek -> _window_peak returns 0.0 for an empty series, and native_value filters out a 0.0 gap, publishing 0.0. The only producers of the two keys in the whole tree are tests/entities.py fixtures (_gap_load_data), which is why the gap tests stay green against a fake coordinator while the production payload carries neither.

evidence.contention_note: Shared fan-out box, load1 3.30; the metric is a computed advisory figure from a fixed series, immune to contention.

perturbation.change: One-line production edit in coordinator.py _build_data_dict: publish the live power series, e.g. data['heat_pump_power_series'] = <series> and data['house_power_series'] = <series> (the harness injects the two keys, equivalent to the fix taking effect).

findings.metric_definition: The house-power slot's sek_per_month in SensorGapAdvisorSensor._gaps(), with the house-power entity unconfigured, on a real post-solve coordinator payload.
findings.phenomenon_property: A published advisory value must read a key the coordinator publishes; a value read from a key nothing writes is the empty-input fallback for every install.
findings.seam_rule: Enumerate data.get("*_power_series") read sites in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/sensor.py; each key read there must be written by coordinator._build_data_dict.

null_control.note: Same harness with the two series present: gap_house_power_sek_per_month_with_series=30.0. The effect is absent exactly when the series exists, so the 0.0 is a property of the missing keys, not of the ranking function.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py _build_data_dict: publish the rolling house and heat-pump power series under house_power_series and heat_pump_power_series (the live-power window the advisor and the #1269 sensor advisor already read). Roughly two lines plus whatever rolling buffer exists.

findings.title: dhw_setpoint_advisor ships enabled-by-default on a no-DHW install, the one DHW sensor without the gate
findings.claim: DHWSetpointAdvisorSensor is the only hot-water sensor not wrapped in _DHWEntityMixin, so a no-DHW install ships it enabled by default while it is permanently unavailable (1 of 59 sensors), where the five mixin-wrapped DHW entities correctly ship off.
findings.mechanism: _DHWEntityMixin.entity_registry_enabled_default returns dhw_enabled, and its available gates on data['dhw_enabled']; the five entities that inherit it (dhw_cost, dhw_energy, dhw_heating_cost, dhw_heating_schedule, plan_dhw_heating) are therefore disabled by default without DHW. DHWSetpointAdvisorSensor (sensor.py:2361) extends HeatPumpOptimizerSensorBase directly, declares no _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default, and its available requires dhw_advisor.recommended_setpoint, which _build_data_dict emits only when DHW is on.

evidence.unit: DHW-gated sensor entities shipped enabled-by-default on a no-DHW install
evidence.contention_note: Shared fan-out box, load1 4.02; a census count over a frozen clock, immune to contention.

perturbation.change: One-line production edit: wrap DHWSetpointAdvisorSensor in _DHWEntityMixin (class DHWSetpointAdvisorSensor(_DHWEntityMixin, HeatPumpOptimizerSensorBase)).

findings.metric_definition: Count of sensor entities whose registry default is enabled and whose available is False on a no-DHW config but True on a DHW config (DHW-gated yet shipped enabled).
findings.phenomenon_property: A feature-gated entity that is unavailable on every refresh of a no-feature install must ship disabled by default, as every sibling DHW entity does.
findings.seam_rule: Enumerate sensors whose available reads dhw_enabled or dhw_advisor; each must either inherit _DHWEntityMixin or declare _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default=False.

null_control.note: The five _DHWEntityMixin entities ship off without DHW (dhw_entities_off_by_default_without_dhw=5), and the fixed variant flips to False on the no-DHW coordinator (fixed_dhw_setpoint_advisor_enabled_default=False) — so the count of 1 is the gap, not the census method.

reproduction_steps: read RESULT dhw_gated_enabled_by_default=1 (DETAIL dhw_setpoint_advisor) and RESULT fixed_dhw_setpoint_advisor_enabled_default=False
findings.proposed_fix_scope: sensor.py DHWSetpointAdvisorSensor: add _DHWEntityMixin to its bases (or set _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default=False and gate available on dhw_enabled). One line plus the base-class change.

non_findings.claim: Every published leaf of every entity of all five platforms is JSON/orjson-serialisable (no numpy scalar, numpy array, NaN/inf, or non-JSON type), across 9 configs x 2 cycles.
No ENUM sensor publishes a state outside its options, and no MEASUREMENT/TOTAL/TOTAL_INCREASING sensor publishes a non-numeric state, and no TIMESTAMP sensor publishes a non-datetime.
No sensor's unit mismatches its device_class and no device_class/state_class pair violates Home Assistant's DEVICE_CLASS_STATE_CLASSES table.
Every entity_id matches {domain}.heat_pump_optimizer_{translation_key}, is unique, and every translation_key is present in strings.json, en.json and sv.json.
The plan_* prefix that separates plan_space_heating/plan_dhw_heating from the space_heating_*/dhw_* families is a deliberate #1333 grouping, not an accidental split.
non_findings.command: read custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js PLAN_ID_SUFFIXES (lines 1396-1403) and sensor.py class list
non_findings.value: PLAN_ID_SUFFIXES names both forms per family; the card's four headline stats are all plan_* and enabled by default
